checks.title: Time range
checks.detail: Set the dashboard's time window to cover the incident.

checks.title: Decisive panel
checks.detail: Selected ${var.value}, the ${var.field_label} that stood out, so every panel filtered to it.

checks.title: Underlying evidence
checks.detail: Opened the records behind the chart to confirm it.

answer.evidence: The selected ${var.field_label} and the records behind it connect ${truth.finding} to ${truth.scope}.

goals.title: Set the time window
goals.concept: Setting a time range separates the incident from everyday, background activity in every panel at once.
goals.narration: The report says the problem was first noticed ${detected_offset_minutes} minutes ago. Set the dashboard's time window so every panel reaches back to that moment without much older traffic.
goals.reasoning: A tight time range keeps the incident in view without letting older, unrelated data throw off the comparison.
goals.evidence: The results refresh to the window you picked.

demonstration.narration: The report was noticed ${detected_offset_minutes} minutes ago. I'll set the dashboard to the last ${var.window_spelled}, rounded to a five-minute boundary, so every panel covers that moment without older traffic.
demonstration.evidence: Every panel now covers only the last ${var.window_spelled}, including the report from ${detected_offset_minutes} minutes ago. Next, read the panels for the ${var.field_label} that stands out.

drifts.note: You filtered the dashboard before setting its time window; this step is about choosing when to look.

hints: Too short a window misses the report entirely; a much longer one mixes older, normal traffic into every panel.
Use the time picker above the panels; it applies to every panel at once.
Set the range to the last ${var.window_spelled}; Show me can do it for you.

goals.title: Select the value that stands out
goals.concept: Clicking a chart value filters every panel to it, without editing the dashboard.
goals.narration: Find the panel that breaks the incident down by ${var.field_label} and click the value that stands out, so every panel filters to it.
goals.reasoning: A blended total can hide which segment drives the change; the breakdown panel shows it.
goals.evidence: Every panel now shows only the selected value.

demonstration.narration: I'll click the ${var.field_label} that stands out in its panel, so every other panel filters to the same slice.
demonstration.reasoning: A total or blended chart can hide which segment drives a change. Clicking the value that stands out filters every panel to it, without editing the dashboard.
demonstration.evidence: Every panel now filters to ${var.value}, the ${var.field_label} that stood out. Check the records behind the chart before deciding what the pattern means.

drifts.note: You filtered to ${action.value}; check whether that is really the ${var.field_label} that stands out.
You selected ${action.value}; check whether that is really the ${var.field_label} that stands out.

hints: Look for the panel that splits the incident by ${var.field_label}; one value should stand apart.
Click its bar, or open its legend entry's menu and choose Filter for, to filter every panel to it.
Select ${var.value}; Show me can point it out.

goals.title: Check the records behind the chart
goals.concept: A chart is an aggregate; its underlying records show what it actually counted.
goals.narration: Open the records behind the panel, keeping its filter and time, and check that they show what the chart suggests.
goals.reasoning: This verifies that the chart means what the conclusion will claim.
goals.evidence: The underlying records carry the facts behind the chart.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the records behind the chart, with its filter and time intact, to check that they show what the chart suggests.
demonstration.reasoning: A chart can be misread if its formula, buckets or filters are misunderstood. Its underlying records show what it actually counted.
demonstration.evidence: The underlying records match the selected ${var.field_label} and window, so the chart's pattern is real. Together they support: ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Check the chart against the records it counts.
Hover the panel and use Explore in Discover (or Inspect) to see them with the same filter and time.
Open the panel's underlying data; Show me can demonstrate the read-only path.

goals.title: Submit a dashboard-supported conclusion
goals.concept: Cite both the visual pattern and the records behind it.
goals.narration: Record the conclusion without editing or saving the dashboard.
goals.reasoning: A view-only investigation should still produce an evidence chain someone else can follow.
goals.evidence: The response cites the panel and its underlying records.
hints: Sum up what the evidence shows.
Use the coach's answer form: name what you found, its scope, and what the evidence shows.
Submit the finding, scope and conclusion; Show me shows the reference summary.
